question.problem:
The parabola $y={x}^{2}+x+4$ and the line $y=5x$ intersect at the point $P.$ Find the coordinates of $P.$

The coordinates of $P$ are
$(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2}+x+4 \\ y=5x\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x+4 & =5x \\ {x}^{2}-4x+4 & =0 \\ (x-2)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point is $x=2.$

To find the $y$-coordinate of the intersection point, we plug this value into either curve. Let's choose the equation of the line. Substituting $x=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =5x \\  & =5(2) \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the only point of intersection is $(2,10).$
